summary: A lean Knizia area-control and set-collection game where you spread settlers and villages across a shrinking archipelago in two distinct phases. It plays fast, feels tense turn to turn, and rewards efficient positioning more than long-term planning.
praised: Elegant, simple rules for the depth they produce
criticised: Can feel dry or overly abstract for players wanting theme
Limited long-term strategy once the phase-two reset happens

interaction.kind: area-majority contests over shared island resources and blocking expansion paths
interaction.detail: Players place settlers/villages that must connect to the shared lagoon or their own network, and scoring is won by claiming majority on specific resource tiles and islands, so placements are often chosen to deny an opponent a majority or a connection route. Still, most of a turn is your own token placement rather than a direct clash, so the board is shared territory to be contested rather than fought over move-by-move.
interaction.said: unknown — no strong recurring reputation recalled; falling back on mechanics

subsystems: island territorial control (coverage, chains, per-island majority)
sources: resource set bonus (4+/3/2 of a kind)
scoring.how_you_win: The exploration phase ends and is scored once players exhaust their villager pieces, the board resets, and the settlement phase then ends and is scored the same way when pieces run out again; the combined two-phase total decides the winner.
